title: Derivative Rules and the Chain Rule
learning_objectives: Apply the power, sum, product and chain rules
Represent a function together with its derivative as a pair
Verify an analytic derivative against a central-difference estimate
entry_point: power_rule(n); sum_rule(f, df, g, dg); product_rule(f, df, g, dg); chain_rule(f, df, g, dg); sigmoid_of_linear(a, b)
hints: Each rule returns two lambdas, e.g. `(lambda x: f(x) + g(x)), (lambda x: df(x) + dg(x))`.
Chain rule: `dh = lambda x: df(g(x)) * dg(x)` — the outer derivative is evaluated at g(x).
The sigmoid's derivative is `lambda u: sigmoid(u) * (1 - sigmoid(u))`; the linear pair is `(lambda x: a * x + b, lambda x: a)`.

failure_feedback.advice: Return the sum of the functions and the sum of their derivatives.
Evaluate the outer derivative at `g(x)` and multiply by `dg(x)`.
Build the pair with `chain_rule(sigmoid, dsigmoid, linear, dlinear)`.
Use the stable sigmoid from the starter for both the value and the derivative.
